summary:
The Bankruptcy Administration Improvement Act of 2025 (Pub. L. 119-76; S. 3424), enacted February 6, 2025, amends titles 11 and 28 of the U.S. Code to (1) increase chapter 7 trustee compensation, (2) modify and reallocate bankruptcy fees, and (3) extend the terms of certain temporary bankruptcy judgeships.

**Trustee compensation (Section 3).** Section 3(a) amends 11 U.S.C. § 330(b)(1) by striking "$45" and inserting "$105," raising the fixed per-case trustee payment (which, combined with the unchanged $15 under § 330(b)(2), yields $120 per case per the findings). It repeals § 330(e). Section 3(b) directs, notwithstanding any other law, that the remainder of fees collected under 28 U.S.C. § 1930(a)(1)(A) after trustee compensation be deposited as follows: $63.51 to the § 1931 special fund; $25.00 to the special fund under section 10101(b) of the Deficit Reduction Act of 2005; and $51.49 to the United States Trustee System Fund (28 U.S.C. § 589a). Section 3(c) conformingly amends § 589a(b)(1)(A), substituting a fixed "$51.49 of the fees collected in each case" for "40.46 percent," and restructures the deposit-priority provisions of § 589a(f)(1) by striking subparagraphs (B) and (C), redesignating (D) as (B), and changing "Fourth" to "Second."

**Bankruptcy fees (Section 4).** Section 4(a) amends the chapter 11 quarterly-fee provision at 28 U.S.C. § 1930(a)(6)(B): extending the applicable period in clause (i) from "5-year" to "10-year," and in clause (ii) revising the fee formula to "the greater of" 0.4 percent "or" (rather than "and") a rate raised in subclause (II) from 0.8 to 0.9 percent. Section 4(b) extends deposit-period references in § 589a(f) from "2026" to "2031." Section 4(c) provides that, for fiscal years 2026 through 2031, notwithstanding § 589a(b), § 1930(a)(6) fees be deposited per § 589a(f), except that $5,400,000 annually be deposited in the general fund of the Treasury.

**Temporary judgeships (Section 5).** Section 5(a) amends Section 4 of the Bankruptcy Administration Improvement Act of 2020 (28 U.S.C. § 152 note) by striking "5 years" and inserting "10 years" throughout numerous subsections. Section 5(b) makes the same extension to Section 1003(b)(2)(A) of the Bankruptcy Judgeship Act of 2017.

**Effective dates (Section 6).** Amendments generally take effect on the first calendar quarter beginning on or after enactment. Exceptions: Section 3 applies to chapter 7 cases (and chapter 11/12/13 cases converted to chapter 7) commenced on or after the first October 1 after enactment; Section 4 applies to chapter 11 cases commenced or pending as of the first post-enactment quarter and to quarterly fees for disbursements in quarters beginning on or after enactment.

The findings state the Act does not alter chapter 7 filing fees or affect courts' authority to waive fees for indigent individuals.
